mcqs.question: Which of the following statements correctly defines inertia?

options.A: The tendency of an object to resist any change in its state of motion.
options.B: The force required to keep an object moving at a constant speed.
options.C: The product of an object's mass and its acceleration.
options.D: The speed of an object when no forces act on it.

mcqs.answer: The tendency of an object to resist any change in its state of motion.
mcqs.explanation: Inertia is the property of matter that resists changes in its state of rest or uniform motion. Option A captures this definition. Option B confuses inertia with the concept of net force needed for acceleration. Option C describes Newton's second law (F = ma). Option D incorrectly equates inertia with speed.

mcqs.question: A book lying on a table remains at rest. Which statement best explains this observation in terms of inertia of rest?

options.A: The book has no mass, so no force is needed to keep it stationary.
options.B: The book’s inertia resists any change in its state, and no unbalanced external force acts on it.
options.C: Earth’s gravity constantly pushes the book to move, but the book chooses to stay still.
options.D: Friction provides a net force that accelerates the book forward.

mcqs.answer: The book’s inertia resists any change in its state, and no unbalanced external force acts on it.
mcqs.explanation: Inertia of rest means an object at rest will stay at rest unless acted upon by an unbalanced external force. Here, the book’s inertia keeps it stationary because the forces (gravity and normal reaction) are balanced, and there is no net external force. Option A is false because the book does have mass. Option C misinterprets gravity’s role, and option D incorrectly states that friction accelerates the book.

mcqs.question: Which statement correctly compares the inertia of motion of a moving truck and a moving bicycle, both traveling at the same speed on a level road?

options.A: The bicycle has greater inertia of motion because it is moving faster.
options.B: Both have equal inertia of motion because inertia depends only on speed.
options.C: The truck has greater inertia of motion because inertia of motion depends on both mass and speed.
options.D: Neither has inertia of motion when moving at constant speed.

mcqs.answer: The truck has greater inertia of motion because inertia of motion depends on both mass and speed.
mcqs.explanation: Inertia of motion is proportional to the product of mass and velocity (momentum). Even though both have the same speed, the truck’s larger mass gives it a larger momentum, i.e., greater inertia of motion. Option A is wrong because speed is equal. Option B ignores mass. Option D is incorrect; inertia of motion exists for any moving object.

mcqs.question: A spacecraft coasting in deep space with no external forces will continue to move in a straight line. Which statement about its inertia of direction is true?

options.A: Its inertia of direction will cause it to curve around massive bodies automatically.
options.B: Its inertia of direction will keep its velocity vector unchanged unless acted upon by an external force.
options.C: Its inertia of direction will increase its speed over time.
options.D: Its inertia of direction will cause it to stop after a finite time.

mcqs.answer: Its inertia of direction will keep its velocity vector unchanged unless acted upon by an external force.
mcqs.explanation: Inertia of direction, a facet of Newton’s first law, means an object in motion maintains both its speed and direction (i.e., its velocity) unless a net external force acts. Hence the spacecraft will keep moving straight at constant speed. Option A describes gravitational attraction, which is an external force. Option C is false because inertia does not change speed. Option D contradicts the law of inertia.
